<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par128" />{{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלַת־אוֹב|translate=a woman that hath a soothsaying spirit}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=4}}; in the plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי חִצִּים|translate=archers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=23}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי בְרִית|translate=confederates}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי שְׁבוּעָה|translate=sworn supporters}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|v}}
(''c'') Of {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}}, &c.: {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־חַ֫יִל|translate=a hero, warrior}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מֶ֫שֶׁק|translate=heir}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־שָׁנָה|translate=yearling}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=5}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מְאַת שָׂנָה|translate=centum annos natus}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מָ֫וֶת|translate=worthy to die}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=31}} (Luther, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=5}} ''ein Kind des Todes''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּן־הַכּוֹת|translate=worthy to be beaten}}. Feminine, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּת־בְּלִיַּ֫עַל|translate=a wicked woman}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=16}}; frequently also {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ בְּלִיַּ֫עַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי ב׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי ב׳}} and even simply {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִיַּ֫עַל}}, like the Latin ''scelus'' for ''scelestissimus'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=18}}. Plural masculine, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי מֶ֑רִי|translate=children of rebellion}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=25}}. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}} is used poetically of things without life, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־שָׁ֫מֶן|translate=a fat}}, i.e. a fruitful (hill); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּן־לַ֫יְלָה}} i.e. ''grown in a night''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=20}} ''son of the bow'' (i.e. an arrow); so also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי רֶשֶׁף}} = ''sparks'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=7}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}} ''the daughters of song'', probably meaning the individual notes.

There is another use of {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}} or {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי}} to denote membership of a guild or society (or of a tribe, or any definite class). Thus {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הָֽאֱלֹהִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=2}}, 4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֵלִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=7|hidebook=1}}) properly means not ''sons of god''(''s''), but beings of the class of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=אֵלִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵיֽ־הַנְּבִיאִיס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=35}} (singular in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=14}}) persons ''belonging to the guild of prophets''; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הָֽרַקָּתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=3|verse=8}} ''one of the guild of apothecaries'', cf. 3:31 where {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הַצֹּֽרְפִים}} is to be read. Similarly {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי שִׁלֵּשִׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=23}} are most probably not ''great-grandsons'' but ''grandsons'', i.e. those belonging to the third generation. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הַגֵּֽרְשֻׁנִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=27}} f. ''Gershonites'', {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=19}}, &c., ''Kohathites''; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי קֶ֫דֶם|translate=dwellers in the East}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|w}}
3. Special mention must be made of the not infrequent idiom by which adjectives (sometimes also ordinals, see {{GHGpar|134|o}}) are added in the genitive, like substantives, rather than as attributes in the same state, gender, and number as the noun which they qualify; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=צִיצַת נֹבֵל|translate=the flower of that which fades}}, for which verse 1 has {{GHGheb|text=צִיץ נֹבֵל|translate=the fading flower}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=17}} (?), 52:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (but {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָן}} may be a substantive), 78:49; also the use of {{GHGheb|text=רַע}} as a substantive, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=14}} b, 6:24 ({{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת רַע}}), &c., analogous to the New Testament phrase ὁ οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀδικίας, Luke 16:8, and the French ''un homme de bien''.<ref>On the other hand, in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=17}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=10}}, &c., there is no apparent reason why the Masora requires the construct state instead of the absolute; hence {{GHGheb|text=חֵיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=2}} and {{GHGheb|text=גֵּיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}} must be intended as forms of the absolute state, shortened in consequence of their close connexion.</ref>—Finally, an adverb (treated as a substantive) may likewise be used as an epexegetical genitive; cf. {{GHGheb|text=דְּמֵי חִנָּם|translate=blood shed without cause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=31}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|x}}
'''3.''' The epexegetical genitives include finally the numerous nearer definitions which follow the coustruct state of adjectives (and of active and passive participles, or verbal adjectives, cf. {{GHGpar|116|f}}–l). For, while the word of nearer definition is added to the verb in the accusative (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חָלָה אֶת־רַגְלָיו|translate=he was diseased in his feet}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=23}}), it may, with participles and verbal adjectives, be either in the accusative<section end="par128" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
